not_empty_record.says: true when a raw record has any field with content; a blank line is not a record

with_index.says: a raw record with its 1-based data-record index; the index counts records after the header, blank lines included, so quoted newlines never shift it

data_records.says: the data records of a parsed file with indices, blank lines dropped

drop_first_item.says: the list without its first item

item_after.says: the item one position after the index in a

transform.says: the whole batch result for a supplier file: lexical outcome, header check, validation report, and the normalised snapshot when accepted

run.says: the batch entry point: transform, show the report on the panel, and export the snapshot only when accepted

clamp_to.says: x held between lo and hi inclusive; never use it to hide an unavailable quantity

same_text.says: 1 when the two texts in a pair are the same scalar sequence, else 0

unique_text.says: true when no two texts in the list are the same scalar sequence; the empty list is unique

is_sorted_pair.says: 1 when the text in a is not after the text in b

min_text.says: the smallest text in a non-empty list by scalar sequence

is_min_of.says: true when the text in a is not after any text in the list in b

digits_fit.says: true when a digit string, without its leading zeros, denotes a number no larger than the exact maximum; decided by length and then by text comparison, never by converting

parse_decimal_nat.says: the value of a string of ASCII digits; refuses anything else and refuses a value that would leave the exact range, before converting

header_ok.says: true when the header is exactly SKU,NAME,PRICE_VND,QTY_ON_HAND

field_problem.says: the first problem with a raw record, as a located diagnostic {index field problem}, or none

problem_count.says: 1 when a diagnostic names a problem, else 0

has_problem.says: true when a diagnostic names a problem

normalize_record.says: a validated raw record as a product: SKU kept, NAME preserved, PRICE_VND and QTY_ON_HAND as exact numbers; the validation guarantees the conversions cannot refuse

index_of.says: the data-record index of a raw record

sku_dup.says: 1 when the two raw records in a pair carry the same SKU text and are different records, else 0

involved_in_dup.says: true when the raw record in a shares its SKU with another record in the list in b

raw_of.says: the raw record of a pair

duplicate_indices.says: the data-record indices of every record whose SKU appears more than once, in file order

validate_snapshot.says: every located field diagnostic, the duplicate-SKU indices, and whether the snapshot is accepted: accepted only when there are records, no field problems and no duplicates

index_ok.says: 1 when a raw record's index is at least 1

accepted_of.says: the accepted flag of a validation result

sku_before.says: true when the product in a sorts strictly before the product in b by SKU

count_before.says: how many products in the list in b sort before the product in a; with unique SKUs this is its position

swap.says: the pair with a and b exchanged

at_position.says: the product in the list in b whose position by SKU order is the index in a; the SKUs must be unique for positions to be unique

position_is.says: true when the product in a has the wanted position within the list carried in b

normalize_snapshot.says: the accepted snapshot as products sorted by SKU; refuses a snapshot that validate_snapshot does not accept

paddle_ok.says: true when the paddle is inside the field

ball_ok.says: true when the ball is between the side walls, below the ceiling, and within the speed ceiling

move_paddle.says: the paddle after one tick: by its intent, or toward its target when one is given, at PADDLE_SPEED, stopping at the edges and at the target

move_ball.says: the ball one tick on, reflected in place by the side walls and the ceiling; the floor is open

paddle_hit.says: the ball after the paddle check: a ball moving down whose box overlaps the paddle box sits on the paddle top, faster upward, with sideways speed from where it struck; hit says whether that happened

cell_ok.says: 1 when a brick's row and column are inside the wall

brick_cx.says: the x of a brick's centre

brick_cy.says: the y of a brick's centre

brick_visit.says: one brick after the ball's visit: a is the ball, b the brick; an intact overlapped brick is removed and the hit axis recorded as the axis of least penetration, y when tied

brick_of.says: the brick part of a visit result

hit_x.says: 1 when a visit hit on the x axis

hit_y.says: 1 when a visit hit on the y axis

new_brick.says: an intact brick at a cell

wall.says: a fresh wall: 5 rows of 6 intact bricks, in row-major order

wall_ok.says: true when the wall has exactly 30 bricks on valid cells

bricks_visit.says: every brick after the ball's visit, in the same order

bounce_off_bricks.says: the ball with vy reversed once when any visit hit on y, and vx reversed once when any hit on x

lost.says: true once the ball's top edge has passed the floor

on_paddle.says: the ball resting on the paddle, ready to launch; the serve angle comes from the launch count, so play is deterministic

G1.says: the paddle stays inside the field

G2.says: bricks never come back and the wall keeps its 30 cells; only a restart to the title rebuilds the wall

G3.says: the score is the number of removed bricks

G4.says: a life is lost once, exactly when the ball exits; only a restart to the title gives lives back

G5.says: the ball never passes the speed ceiling

burst_ok.says: 1 when a burst is well formed

state_ok.says: true when the game state is well formed: a known phase, the paddle in the field, the ball within walls and speed limits, a 30-cell wall, score equal to removed bricks, lives 0–3

initial.says: the title screen: a fresh wall, the paddle centred, the ball resting on it, three lives, nothing launched

young.says: true while a burst is still shown

aged.says: the bursts one tick older, the finished ones dropped

removed_now.says: true when a visit removed a brick this tick

burst_at.says: a fresh burst at a removed brick's centre

play_tick.says: one tick of play: the paddle moves, the ball moves and reflects off walls, the paddle strike, brick hits, then loss or win

serve_tick.says: one tick while the ball waits on the paddle: the paddle moves and the ball rides it; nothing else changes

on_tick.says: a tick: play and serve advance; title, paused, won and lost stand still, so a delayed host frame can never move the game by itself

on_launch.says: the player launches: from the title or from the paddle the ball leaves upward; counted, so the next serve angle differs

on_pause.says: pause freezes play or serve exactly where it is

on_resume.says: resume continues from the frozen state; no time passed for the game

on_restart.says: restart: exactly the initial state, whatever came before

event_ok.says: true when an event carries the fields its kind needs

step.says: one event applied to the game

brick_shape.says: the rectangle of an intact brick in its row colour, or nothing for a removed one

burst_shape.says: a ring that grows and fades over a burst's life

overlay.says: the words over the field for the phase: title, serve, paused, won, lost; nothing during play
out: Move: ← → or drag · Launch: space or tap
All 30 bricks cleared · R or tap to play again
· R or tap to play again

view.says: the draw list: field, bricks, bursts, paddle, ball, score and lives, and the phase overlay

sound_of.says: the sound for what just happened, or none

frame.says: the entry point: one event in, the next state out, the field drawn and the sound played; on a refusal nothing is drawn and the host keeps the old state
